newsitem.title: USA: U.S. "deeply concerned" by troubles in Albania.
newsitem.headline: U.S. "deeply concerned" by troubles in Albania.

text.p: The United States said on Tuesday it was "deeply concerned" about growing disorder in Albania over a financial scandal, and called on both protesters and authorities to refrain from violence.

Thousands of people facing ruin in Europe's poorest state following the collapse of a string of pyramid investment schemes have taken to the streets in recent weeks, leading to clashes with police in Tirana and other cities.
"The United States government is deeply concerned about recent developments in Albania," said State Department spokesman Glyn Davies.
"While we understand the motivation for these protests, we urge that leaders in the affected communities issue a call against violence," Davies said in a statement.
But he also called on Albanian authorities to permit peaceful demonstrations, saying Washington was "deeply troubled" by reports of beatings and intimidation of opposition figures and journalists.
Davies repeated a call the State Department made last October for a new constitution to be drafted in Albania, followed by free and fair national elections.

Washington originally supported Albanian President Sali Berisha, who took power in the formerly Stalinist Balkan state in 1992. But it became disillusioned after parliamentary elections last year that were widely criticised for irregularities.
Berisha must seek a fresh term in office in a vote in parliament by April 9.
